preconditions.description: The number of queries q is between 1 and 150,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= n <= 300000 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) >= 2])
preconditions.description: Each query's tree has n vertices where n is between 2 and 300,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == n - 1 for n, edges in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()], [line.strip().split() for line in stdin.splitlines() if not line.strip().isdigit()]))
preconditions.description: Each query's tree has exactly n-1 edges, forming a connected acyclic graph.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= n for n, edges in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()], [line.strip().split() for line in stdin.splitlines() if not line.strip().isdigit()]) for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects vertices with valid indices between 1 and n.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one integer per query.

postconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(line) <= n for n, line in zip([int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i])]] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)), stdout.splitlines()[i//(n+1)]) if line.strip().isdigit())
postconditions.description: Each output integer is a valid subtree size between 2 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(any(subtree_size == n for subtree_size in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i])]] if n >= 2)
postconditions.description: If the entire tree is a good subtree, the output is n.

postconditions.expression: all(any(subtree_size == 2 for subtree_size in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i])]] if n >= 2)
postconditions.description: If no good subtree larger than 2 exists, the output is 2.

postconditions.expression: all(any(subtree_size == max_possible for subtree_size in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]) for n, edges, max_possible in zip([int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i])]], [line.strip().split() for line in stdin.splitlines() if not line.strip().isdigit()], [max_good_subtree_size(n, edges) for n, edges in zip([int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1) for n in [int(stdin.splitlines()[i])]], [line.strip().split() for line in stdin.splitlines() if not line.strip().isdigit()])]))
postconditions.description: The output for each query is the maximum size of a good subtree, where a good subtree is a connected subgraph that can be represented by intersecting segments.
